newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on foreign fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on foreign fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday amid active inflows of foreign funds for the rebounding stock market, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.540 against Wednesday's T$27.570 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$278 million.
"Many think the Taiwan dollar should fall to reflect the impact of the pork export ban, but it simply rose because of active foreign fund inflows for the stock market," said one dealer.
Taiwan announced on March 20 that it was banning exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of the deadly contagious hog foot and mouth disease.
The pork export ban will reduce Taiwan's overall exports by 1.34 percent according to 1996 figures, thus cutting the island's trade surplus and pressuring the Taiwan dollar to fall, dealers said.

On Thursday, the stock index gained 60.38 points or 0.75 percent to close at 8,089.71 for the second consecutive rebound following a big decline caused by the export ban and unconfirmed reports that rival China was planning new war games.
Dealers also attributed the local dollar's appreciation in part to the greenback's weakness on Thursday in Tokyo and other Asian markets.
For Friday, a T$27.52-27.56 range was seen.
